evals.name: coverage-first
evals.prompt: I just rewrote the description of our deploy skill. Before I open the PR, how do I check that it still triggers on the requests people actually type, and what would the run cost? Give me the exact commands, don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Checks eval coverage with repo-skill-evals --list, then runs a trigger-only pass with runs 1 and a cost ceiling, and compares before and after on the same cases.
assertions: Runs repo-skill-evals --list (or names eval coverage) before scoring anything
Proposes a --trigger-only run with a bounded cost (--max-cost-usd or --runs 1)
Says the description, not the prompt, is what to fix when the skill does not fire

evals.name: sandbox-safe-prompts
evals.prompt: Our on-call skill's evals keep failing with errors about not being able to reach the hosts. Should I give the eval runner SSH access? What would you change instead? Just explain, no commands needed.
evals.expected_output: Explains that runs are sandboxed without hosts, credentials or a checkout, so prompts should ask for the plan, exact commands or a decision and assertions should check those; does not grant the runner access.
assertions: Says eval runs are sandboxed with no live hosts, credentials or repository checkout
Recommends rewriting the prompts to ask for a plan, commands or a decision rather than granting access
Does not recommend giving the runner SSH or real credentials

evals.name: retained-evidence-before-repeat
evals.prompt: Use the skill-evals workflow to advise on this evaluation, using only the supplied facts and without executing commands or contacting services. Two weeks ago candidate A was rejected: same source, model, suite and grader as today; score 2/3 with three failed hypotheses. Its scratch worktree is gone, but a protected report and raw evidence survive on another host. I want to try the same changes again and delete the failed results after cleanup. Give the next actions and the retention/publication boundary. Do not launch a new experiment.
assertions: The proposed plan checks retained evidence and shared registry/memory before repeating, and recognizes that a missing local worktree or local-store miss does not erase another host's effort. Actual tool execution is forbidden and is not required to pass.
The advice calls for a recorded change in conditions or a reason for additional samples before repeating rejected changes, and says failed/discarded evidence must remain for at least 90 days.

The proposed bounded summary includes run identity and owning host/path/report references, with raw traces and credentials kept out of public source. This is a proposed publication boundary; no actual publication is required.

evals.name: harness-independent-cases
evals.prompt: Our skill evals need to run with any harness. We already use Claude and Codex and now want OpenCode. Should I rewrite the prompts, give the evals new credentials, or make another plugin-shaped test suite? Explain the integration and verification steps without executing commands or invoking a model.
assertions: Keeps one shared set of prompts, assertions and fixtures instead of creating harness-specific copies.
Places native execution and authentication in a caller-selected adapter; mentions --runner NAME with --adapter EXECUTABLE or the versioned adapter contract.

Requires native skill-loading evidence, model and grader provenance, and capability/budget verification before claiming the new harness is supported; does not claim all harnesses are already integrated.
Does not grant eval definitions authority to choose credentials, invoke shell/network tools or rewrite permission scopes.
